newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay bourse chief uncertain about market sops.
newsitem.headline: Bombay bourse chief uncertain about market sops.

text.p: The chief of India's leading stock exchange said on Thursday he is uncertain whether the government is likely to announce any major measures to cheer capital markets.
"Quite frankly, the situation is very fluid," M.G. Damani, president of the BSE, told Reuters.
He said stock exchanges were bound to fall if the government did not, as widely expected in the market, announce a large package of measures this week to shore up capital markets.
"The government will have to face the music if the market slumps," Damani said.
He said the degree of the fall would depend on what Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda says before he leaves for the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland on Friday.
"We'll have to see whether he buys more time again until the budget. It depends on the statement he makes," Damani said.

He said market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was likely to make announcements about a new takeover code and clear a stock lending scheme at its board meeting later in the day.
But he did not see SEBI making any announcements on the buy back of shares -- a move awaited by the market.
"I don't think it is in the power of SEBI. The Companies Act has to be amended to introduce buy backs and SEBI cannot do that," Damani said.
